directive.thread_id: film repository port 2026-11-05, lane film-tools: the narrator tools of a film
directive.quote: Finish the port of the film repository so it can be retired: move each job to its correct home, porting the correct parts one to one and never rebuilding from scratch what already worked; move the code byte for byte, then make what it fixed arguments and settings.

targets.baseline_commit_message: check-every-claim-against-its-facts-and-sources: a film's fact gate, source extracts and world reader, moved byte for byte

preserve: World reads lists.json, rows/<list>.json and relations.json into lists, rows, kinds, entities, facts and relations
quote_problem: a fact's words at its transcript second (6 ms) or in its file line
verify: row shapes, field kinds, choices, links, kinds, quotes, relation roles and words, entities with no fact, and the counts
allowed_deltas: the world folder is an argument instead of where the file sat
verify returns (ok, lines) instead of printing
resolve() with path_map for paths written on another computer
the query, drawing and loading commands of the film's world graph are not part of the claim check and are not ported here
banned_substitutions: a second world reader in this folder
_paths: The source lives in a private repository, so it is named by the BLAKE3 identity of its path (path_multihash); a checkout of that repository beside this one finds it. Lines holding a person's name or a private path are left out of the sources (each source names its lines), so they never reach this public repository; the first source is the byte copy. The source is the reader part of the film's world graph (lines 29-196 at its commit); that file belongs to the film's world data, whose lane moves it out of the film repository.
